sections.title: Claims and evidence
findings: Proposal document read by reasoning layer: yes

Requested: Treasury withdrawal to fund the OpenZeppelin Stack for Cardano, including reference implementations, a contracts library, security retainer, developer tools, documentation, and enablement/co-marketing.
Recipient: Intersect as administrator for an OpenZeppelin-led delivery engagement

Deliverables: Three reference implementations: Cardano Liquid Staking Protocol, Self-Repaying Loans Protocol, and Tokenized Money Market Fund., OpenZeppelin Contracts Library for Cardano with audited components and documentation., Contracts Wizard, UI Builder, AI-enhanced development tools, and Cardano documentation., 22 researcher-weeks of security capacity, audits, reviews, penetration testing, and published reports., Developer enablement and co-marketing activities including tutorials, workshops, demos, community sessions, and a Cardano network page.
Deadline/expiry: Twelve months across four quarterly milestones from October 1, 2026 to September 30, 2027, commencing after the legal contract is signed.

Claim (economic, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): The proposal requests a total withdrawal of 11,787,063 ada, consisting of 11,443,750 ada for delivery and a 343,313 ada Intersect administration fee.
Claim (economic, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): The delivery budget is stated as USD $1,831,000 over 12 months, calculated at a reference rate of USD $0.16 per ada.

Claim (technical, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): The project will deliver three production-ready Cardano reference implementations for liquid staking, self-repaying loans, and a tokenized money market fund.

Claim (technical, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): The project will create a secure, audited, documented contracts library for Cardano with components such as access control, cryptographic utilities, DeFi primitives, governance, credentials, multi-signature tools, vesting, messaging, and a proposed contract ABI.

Claim (technical, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): OpenZeppelin states that all code will be released open source, with milestone criteria requiring public GitHub repositories under MIT license and OpenZeppelin tooling under AGPL 3.0.

Claim (technical, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): The security retainer commits 22 researcher-weeks over 12 months for audits, full-stack reviews, penetration testing, AI-security support, and publication of security findings and reports.
missing: Independent evidence for: OpenZeppelin claims its existing contracts ecosystem has processed over $36 trillion in value transferred, supports $110B+ TVL importing its contracts, has about 85% market share in top 50 DeFi protocols, and receives about 590K weekly NPM downloads.
Independent evidence for: OpenZeppelin discloses that it has not received ada from the Cardano Treasury within the prior 24 months and has not received Project Catalyst funding.
sections.conclusion: Each claim must map to replayable public evidence; proposer assertions alone are not enough for confidence.

treasury_capacity.caveat: Set by an Info governance action. Info actions change no ledger state and can NEVER be enacted -- they always expire -- so no formally ratified NCL exists or can exist. This is the strongest available public chain evidence: an anchor document byte-verified against its on-chain blake2b-256 hash, covering the current epoch, whose voting CLOSED with a majority of participating DRep stake. It is NOT enacted ledger state, and the majority may fall short of the supermajority other action types require. Published with every treasury rationale that relies on it.
